featured_reviews.name: Prabhupada Sarangi
featured_reviews.review_text: Recently visited Third Wave Coffee and had a really comfortable experience overall. The café has a calm and easygoing atmosphere that makes it a good place to sit back and relax for a while. The interiors were simple, modern, and well maintained without feeling too crowded or noisy. Coffee quality was genuinely good, with fresh taste and proper preparation, and the food options were decent as well. Service was smooth, and the staff handled orders politely and efficiently. featured_reviews.name: Karan Thapar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually enjoy Third Wave for the service, but this visit was a letdown. The staff member (choosing not to name him) at the counter was quite nonchalant and dismissive when I checked on my order. In fact, the cleaning staff was more pleasant to interact with. My order took over 35-40 minutes to arrive; when I followed up at the 25-minute mark, I was told to just go sit down and wait for it without much of an apology. The slow pace seemed to be a frustration for other customers as well.

Update: Gave this place way too many chances. They got my orders wrong. They took my bags away when I stepped out for a couple of minutes. Never compensated for giving me wrong sizes, got no resolution on the app either. Never expected this from third wave. I don't recommend going there anymore. I used to come here for their amazing staff/service, comfort and good coffee. I'm afraid neither of them exist now.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Love & Latte Juhu
लव & लत्ते जुहू

April 2025:
The outdoor bathroom is absolutely depressing. And they have only one bathroom. The entire cafe has a "faded glory" feel to it. While it's airconditioned, there's an extensive outer-seating area, the music is generic but relaxing, the sofas are comfortable (but need a deep-cleaning!!), and the Flat White ☕ was strong and made how I like it, I didn't find this space comfortable enough to return to. I'm guessing the main clientele are locals...and since it's the heart of Juhu, it's a mostly well-off (💰!) crowd. And, like the rich in most places, some of the clientele don't know how to behave in public: overly loud and bombastic, in both looks and speech, looking like walking billboards for various logos, while also socially awkward. 😆😁
4 Stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐, mainly for the (long-suffering!) staff!

featured_reviews.name: Raveena Chopra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Honestly, I feel like this place is a waste of space. They can manage things so much better. The servers are sweet, however. Few pointers below:

1) we ordered the kitkat chocolate donut. It was literally a bun with a LOT of chocolate and the Kit Kat was moist and not at all crunchy. They heated the Kit Kat with their so called “donut”.
2) The only highlight of the place is ministry of games but that too, is horribly managed. The tables have velvet covers with stains of food that cannot be removed after every serving. Ppl drop food and it gets soaked into the cover.
3) The coffee was super sweet and seemed like something I could make at home.
4) I understand the concept of a basement having games, which is super cool but they could’ve worked on the ambience. There are black curtains out of nowhere.

Overall, had a fun time only cause of the games, they have a good variety.

featured_reviews.name: Nirel Dlima
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a really unpleasant experience at this coffee shop today. The security guard (bald gentleman at the entrance) was extremely rude and disrespectful. I had parked my scooter outside and before I could even walk in, he abruptly asked if I was a Zomato rider — in a very dismissive and insulting tone.

What makes this more disappointing is that this isn’t my first visit. I actually enjoy the coffee and food here and have been coming back because of that. However, almost every time I visit, this particular gentleman behaves rudely, which completely ruins the overall experience.

As a paying customer, basic courtesy and respect should be a given. I hope the management takes this seriously and ensures their staff is trained to speak with customers politely. Repeated behaviour like this leaves a very bad impression despite the otherwise good food and coffee.

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text:
The coffee house in itself was very small for takeaway. But we initially came just for the takeaway as there was no seating available on a busy weekend night. After picking up the items bought we were lucky enough to be seated on their outdoor seating area which also happens to be a smoking allowed zone.
Banana chips, sealed glass bottles were provided complementary on every table. Seating was comfortable and it was windy too. But the traffic on the road and the honking of vehicles (that are extremely closeby on the road next to the outdoor seating area) were a deterrent to a lovely experience otherwise.
There's a buzzer provided at each desk to call the staff when in need. Menu is to be scanned from the QR and hence the order placing experience was smooth. We had tried their Baked Pav Bhaji, Paneer Calzone, Filter coffee, Vietnamese iced latte, chocolate tartlet, chocolate namelaka sihi and filter kaapi misu Sihi. The Savory food items are all worth trying especially the baked pav bhaji was a melt-in-mouth and tasted fresh. The Vietnamese iced latte is skippable and filter coffee could have been better. Sihi, however, was the most anticipated item that has disappointed. The portion size was too small and the taste didn't quite impress us. Chocolate namelaka tasted more like a thickened mousse than a cheesecake. We couldn't try Papparoti as they were out of stock. Will be back to try more from their menu,possibly in the indoor seating area this time.

featured_reviews.name: Treesa Jose
featured_reviews.review_text: Really good bistro serving variety coffee, and fusion small plates / light food. Affordable price for the location they're in (close to Juhu beach). It's a small place and finding a table in evenings may need waiting. Tartlets are good especially their kacha nimbu. Really enjoyed the matka cheesecake (filter-kapi flavour). Pasta, pizza, sandwich, rolls all available in a limited menu and all are fusion. The ambience and vibe is good.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Gogri
featured_reviews.review_text: I absolutely love the coffee at Ettarra! I often order their Mocha and Hazelnut Frappe — both are amazing. The concept of offering banana chips and letting customers taste the coffee before ordering is such a nice touch, and those little tasting buckets are adorable! However, the service felt a bit slow — it took quite some time to get both the tasting sample and my final order. Definitely try the baked Vada Pav, and the Kappiccino is an absolute must-have! Also, their branding — from the cups and glasses to the water bottles — is spot on.

Their top floor seating is the best and would recommend the same. Service was excellent and the staff was really polite.

We ordered for Iced Mocha and Iced filter coffee along with Macaroons (Strawberry, Lemon and Filter coffe flavours).
Iced filter coffee was just bang on and Macaroons are a must must try for sure😋
Iced mocha was good too with good mix of chocolate and filter coffee!

A must visit coffee place if you are around Juhu and they also serve savoury food items and maybe next time will try for sure!

Overall, a great experience and worth multiple visits!❤️

featured_reviews.name: Khushi Porwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried a few dishes at Earth Cafe and here’s my take:

🍝 Pink Sauce Pasta with Garlic Bread
Creamy, comforting, and well-balanced. The sauce had a nice richness without being too heavy, and the garlic bread was perfectly crisp. A solid crowd-pleaser.

🥑 Avocado Toasts
Fresh, chunky avocado with a good crunch from the toast. Loved the seasoning and presentation—simple but done right.

🍟 Seasoned Fries
Crispy, well-seasoned, and addictive. Perfect side to munch on while chatting.

Overall food: 8/10 — genuinely good and satisfying.

But… the space
The place feels quite congested. Tables are very close to each other, so you can easily hear nearby conversations, which takes away from the experience.

Location reality check
Getting to Juhu itself can be a task—traffic can be a bit of a mood killer.

Final verdict:
Great food, but go prepared for a slightly cramped and noisy vibe.

featured_reviews.name: Dipti Shahani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Earth Cafe @ Juhu last week with friends and we ordered several items from the menu. Everything we tried was incredibly tasty! 😋 The food, service, and atmosphere were all fantastic.
Recommending a few things with images of what we ordered.
If your a pasta lover do try their penne pink sauce pasta, veggilicious pizza was too good.
We called for their salted fries crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
Ruby Red was 1 healthy drink i truly enjoyed.
Hummus platter serves 3 kinds of dips!
We ended this with Hazelnut choco cake (bitter chocolate)
Earth bar (which was average) and carrot walnut cake again a very good healthy desert option!

This place has such a cute and colorful atmosphere! 🌈 We visited with a child, and she absolutely loved the experience. The hanging teddy bears were mesmerizing for all of us.🐻💕

featured_reviews.name: Saif Ashrafi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Earth Cafe recently and absolutely loved the experience! We ordered the Signature Chocolate Cake, Los Angeles Sandwich, Mushroom Kimbap, and a Falafel Wrap — everything was super yummy and fresh.
The chocolate cake was rich and perfectly moist. The sandwich was filling, and the mushroom kimbap was really flavorful. The falafel wrap was packed with protein and veggies, which made the whole meal feel satisfying but not heavy.
The ambience is such a good vibe — very aesthetic, cozy, and perfect for pictures. The teddy and heart decor adds a really cute touch. Overall, great food + great atmosphere. Definitely coming back! alsoo their decorations according to famous festives are on point and appreciated

featured_reviews.name: Where My Fork Goes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Earth Café has a really adorable ambience, decorated with teddy bears, making it a perfect spot for friend outings or cute dates. It’s a pure vegan café, and they also offer vegan milk options for beverages, which is a big plus.

The service is good and the place is genuinely beautiful. We tried their hot chocolate with almond milk, and it was absolutely yum.

Highly recommend this café if you’re looking for a cozy vegan spot. Also, a small tip—the staff member at the door is great at clicking pictures, so don’t hesitate to ask for a memorable photo. 📸✨

featured_reviews.name: Honest Table India
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a very nice cafe giving calm vibes.
They have a nice vegetarian menu with a few vegan options as well.
In beverages they don't have regular milk, just plant based milk.
Food menu is pretty vast.
I think they should shift their focus towards reducing waste as well, and include re-usable straws and cloth napkins instead of paper napkins.
Otherwise nice service, pretty hospitable staff.
They did lack a few ingredients making a few items from the menu impossible to make.

featured_reviews.name: ChikkuThisSide
featured_reviews.review_text:
The café is good but a bit expensive. I mainly visited for the teddy Christmas décor, which was really beautiful and the ambience was nice. The food was good, and the rest of the staff was polite and helpful.

However, one issue spoiled the experience. After finishing our meal, a person (maybe the manager) asked us to leave our place as new customers were arriving, which was understandable. But while we were clicking photos inside the café, he again asked us to leave, which felt rude—especially since other customers were allowed to sit and take photos even after finishing their meals.

Apart from this behavior, everything else was good.

featured_reviews.name: Devika Bharadwaj
featured_reviews.review_text: This branch does great disservice to the rest of the Earth Cafes. It's pet tolerant, not friendly at all. The service is too slow. A simple amaranth bowl took over 45-50 minutes to get. The staff could be better trained in customer service. I am not going again to this one. BKC and Churchgate ones are both so much better.

Aromas Cafe and Bistro - A Perfect Spot to Relax and Indulge in Juhu

I like early start restaurants, this one opens at 8 am, so points to it for that. It’s a size ‘S’ place - that too coz of the mezzanine floor - so best to book and go. The whole place has a quaint look and warm ambience.

So, it was 6 of us and we ordered 7 dishes and orange juice.

The chicken and egg roll were tasty, accompanied by a fresh and slightly sweet tomato and onion chutney. They gave sweet potato fries with it; I would have preferred if they gave a choice between regular and sweet potatoes.

The English breakfast was as it should be. The hash browns were crunchy.

The spicy mutton keema with pao was ok. Have had better.

It’s an add on which you have to pay for. It’s a peev that my kids have with all places serving waffles and pancakes without chocolate sauce or Nutella. But that not withstanding, the taste was great.

Now coming to the 2 things we didn’t like. The chicken croffles, looked like batter fried chicken breast on a waffle and it looked too dark as if deep fried for too long and didn’t taste well. The other thing was that the juices turned out to be too expensive. That glass cost ₹450 without taxes. Nearly equivalent to a dish. That was too much. And for that size of glass ₹200 or ₹250 would have been good.

So apart from that, the rest of the food was good and it is a quaint and cost place to go to with friends and family.

Some places you visit for food, and some places you visit for the entire feeling, Fables in Juhu is definitely the second one. The moment you enter, it feels warm, cozy, and beautifully different. The book-themed décor, with pages and novels creatively stacked around, gives such a charming and aesthetic vibe. We started with their drinks and honestly, each one was impressive. The Penne in Spicy Arrabbiata had the perfect balance of spice and richness. The BBQ Cottage Cheese Pizza was cheesy and satisfying, while the Potato Corn Jalapeño Steak Sizzler arrived sizzling hot and tasted just as good as it looked.

And of course, we couldn’t leave without dessert. The Hazelnut Chocolate Mousse was smooth and rich, and the Tiramisu was soft, creamy, and absolutely yummy the perfect way to end the meal.

A special mention to Mr. Sudesh for his excellent hospitality and attentive service. He made sure everything was smooth and comfortable for us.

If you’re looking for a place in Juhu that offers good food, great drinks, and a cozy aesthetic vibe, Fables is definitely worth checking out.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant lad
featured_reviews.review_text: Dropped by this iconic place yesterday for lunch and we really loved it. Talking about the ambience firstly, fable have got indoor as well as outdoor dining areas, both of which look chic and aesthetic. All white decor with pretty retro elements and rustic corners gives you a perfect European cafe feeling. Coming to the F&B,  in drinks we tried Ferrero Rocher milkshake which was chocolaty and thick. From their coolers, we tried a couple of drinks like Watermelon & Basil, Pomegranate & Basil and lastly a virgin muddy mojito which was a classic virgin mojito made using brown sugar. All the coolers were super refreshing and we would totally recommend trying them out as they would be a perfect option to sip on this summer. From their breakfast menu, we tried the Chicken and Egg Sandwich in focaccia. Hands down one of the finest sandwich we have tried off late. Loaded with flavours and that super soft bread made every bite yum! We also tried their Teriyaki Chicken pizza which we had the option to choose from a thin/thick crust. We went with thick crust and it was fluffy, airy and very well made. The toppings were quite generous and this pizza would easily suffice 2-3 average eaters for a meal. Upon servers recommendation, we also tried their truffle mac n cheese which was served piping hot and it was super cheesy and had that evident earthy and musky flavour of truffle making it a rich and indulgent one. Lastly, we tried their stuffed chicken breast which was a chicken breast stuffed with spinach and mushrooms and served with mashed potatoes and sauteed veggies along with mushroom jus. An absolutely wholesome meal for one person.  For our sweet tooth cravings, we tried Philadelphia baked Cheesecake which was fresh and had that perfect melt-in-the-mouth texture and it was topped with blueberry compote making it even better.  A must try and we highly recommend trying this one. We also tried their Tiramisu which was good too having a perfect balance of sweetness and that bitter kick from the espresso. It was very well layered and would totally recommend it if your palate wants to have something that's not extremely sweet. Hospitality at Fable is 10/10! Captain Pramod made sure everything was on time and delivered the lovely service. Fable is truly one of those places where you can get in for a quick breakfast, slow lunches or even for dinner dates. This place has got you covered for all with their wide spread food options. We will surely visit again super soon.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka
featured_reviews.review_text:
### **Review for Prithvi Café**
Prithvi Café is legendary for its vibe and history, but if I’m being honest, the food felt a bit overhyped. It’s a great spot to hang out, but the flavors were a hit-or-miss for me :(

So, I was leaving for out of India but just wanted to explore this cafe before leaving as I will be missing Indian food a little!
But, I kind of got disappointed with the food. To be honest the dishes I had at airport were better🥲

**The Food Breakdown:**
🌟 Egg Kheema: Just okay. It didn't quite live up to the expectations I had based on the reviews.
🌟 Butter Chicken Thali: This was a letdown. The gravy was **way too sweet**—even for Butter Chicken. It lacked that savory, spicy balance you'd expect.
🌟 Mixed Veg Paratha: One of the better items we ordered. Solid, filling, and tasted fresh.
🌟 Burger (Must Try!): The highlight of the meal. The bun isn't made of maida (refined flour), which gave it a great texture. Definitely worth a try if you want something "healthier" but tasty.
Chocolate Croissant: A decent sweet finish, but nothing groundbreaking.

**Drinks:**
We tried the Blueberry Soda and Masala Soda. Both were refreshing and served as good palate cleansers for the meal.

Go for the atmosphere and the non-maida burgers, but maybe skip the North Indian mains if you aren't a fan of sweet gravies. It's a nice place to chill, just don't expect a culinary masterpiece across the whole menu.

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text: Inspite of visiting a couple of times before, we've never shot pictures to upload in the review as this was a busy place that involved queue system to be seated. Our last visit was on a weekday afternoon and hence we got a table without a wait time. The seating is outdoor and the menu is pocket friendly and extensive. Most of their kitchen seems outdoor and causes fumes,sizzles and fragrances of multiple dishes being cooked. The dining is moderately under dhaded trees and thoroughly placed table fans. The menu and ordering are online while the bill can be paid once your are  about to leave. Service staff are busy but give you attention when needed. Our asked for extra plate/spoon have immediately been fulfilled. The orders once placed have also arrived quick to the table. We've been ordering from this place for years and hence have reordered most of our favorites to enjoy them fresh which include their paratha with dal makhani, red velvet brownie and cookies. Their sulemani chai and masala soda were well made too. No excessive sugars in the beverages that we ordered. Overall it was a nostalgic place for us and being able to dine without a wait time is a plus.

featured_reviews.review_text: The food was top-notch, especially the hummus absolutely delicious! However, the waiting time for a table was too long due to the excessive crowd. featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited **Prithvi Café** and had a really good experience overall. The café has a beautiful, lively ambience with a chilled, artsy vibe — perfect for casual meetups or relaxed meals.

I tried quite a few dishes here:
🍽️ **Amritsari Paratha** – Nicely stuffed, flavorful, and served hot with curd and chutney. The taste was authentic and had a pleasant spicy punch without being overpowering.
🍝 **White Pasta** – Creamy, rich, and perfectly cooked. The sauce was smooth and mildly cheesy, though it could use a little more spice for those who like stronger flavors.
☕ **Hot Coffee & Filter Coffee Ice-Cream** – Both were excellent. The hot coffee was strong and aromatic, while the filter coffee ice-cream was a unique treat — a perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness.
🥭 **Mango Lassi** – Thick, fresh, and refreshing, with a real mango flavor. It paired well with the paratha and gave a nice desi touch to the meal.
🌯 **Chicken Roll** – Juicy, well-marinated, and wrapped in soft bread. Nicely spiced and filling; non-veg lovers will definitely enjoy this.

The **service** was polite and quick despite the crowd. **Pricing** is slightly on the higher side, but the taste and ambience justify it. The **outdoor seating** under trees gives a cozy, café-theatre vibe that’s hard to find elsewhere in Mumbai.

✅ **Overall:** Quite good experience — tasty food, soothing coffee, and vibrant atmosphere. A must-visit if you’re near Juhu, especially for coffee lovers and café enthusiasts

featured_reviews.name: Ritesh Bhagwati
featured_reviews.review_text:
Elementaria Café – So I got hooked to this newly opened joint of Elementaria Café in Juhu. I am regular visitor of the brand in Matunga branch and love their offerings and overall spread of options. I was one of the first customers to this newly open joint and in terms of overall food and drinks quality I relished it.

Luckily we were 4 friends and we tried many things out there as below

•    Vietnamese cake icecream (If I recollect it right) (Rating 3/5) – Thought this would be really interesting given its description but was let down as the cake/pastry was hard even to cut it through spoon. Is it really supposed to be like this I doubt.

•    Hazelnut Red Velvet Tubcake (Rating 5/5) & Intense Chocolate Tubcake (Rating 5/5) – These were lovely little cakes with intense chocolate flavors. The cake around the chocolate liquid was decadent to satisfy with each bite. Loved both.

•    48 Layers Chocolate Cake (Rating 5/5) – This is the best dessert out there IMO! This 48 layer signature cake is so so good that you can actually get it for free if you end up finishing the same in less 10 mins. The entire cake takes about 2 days to make and it weighs roughly 13 pounds.

•    Choco Shake Rating (4/5) – Decent shake offered at their place! Similar to keventers but I think slightly better version imo!

•    Messy Melon icecream (Rating 5/5) – This is another signature item to have at their place. See the picture and you will know why its so sought after item to order. The lovely creation of water melon cut in intricate manner accompanied with delicious melon icecream is a winner! Must order out there.

•    Peri Peri Paneer Hotdog (Rating 4/5) & Chicken Tikka Sandwich (Rating 4/5) – Both offerings were great savory accompaniments with dessert choices they have out there. My personal fav was chicken tikka sandwich which comes with brown bread and generous amount of chicken tikka semi dry gravy. Paneer had unique spiciness but I felt salt somehow lacking in it! Maybe it was my bad day but liked it in general.

•    Marshmellow Hot Chocolate (Rating 5/5) & Hot Mocha with Marshmellow (Rating 5/5)  - Both were WOW! U cant go wrong with these choices usually and this place keeps up with the standards too. Hot chocolate was my personal fav which had the lovely texture of chocolate milk and thick enough to sip in fractions and enjoy till late evenings.

Overall the food and desserts were good, staff even though it was first day were able to manage our orders and others at a same time, the only downside in my opinion of this place is the ambience. It gets extremely uncomfortable to be there inspite of fans at almost each table. They should try adding cooler or something that can make sitting out there pleasant. Hope they can hence for now I rate them 4 for my overall experience.

featured_reviews.name: Ameen Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience here is truly great and has always been a highlight 🌟. I’ve been visiting this restaurant 2-3 times a year for the last 5-7 years, and earlier, the taste they delivered was gold. Back then, they really tried to include everything in their buffet, and the dessert section used to be huge and impressive 🍰🍮.

Now, let’s talk about the breakfast buffet—it’s pretty standard, similar to what you’d find at any 5-star continental breakfast 🍳🥐. They do include a few Indian dishes, but honestly, breakfast here has never excited me since the beginning.

As for dinner, it used to be something I truly looked forward to because of how flavourful and varied the food was 🍽️. However, over the last 2-3 visits, it feels like something is always off—sometimes it’s the salt, sometimes it’s the flavours. The food feels same-same now, and perhaps I’ve become fed up of eating the same dishes repeatedly. There’s nothing new or exciting anymore, and the taste is not extraordinary enough to crave anything specific. I used to love the pizza here; it was one of my favorites. But lately, the taste has literally deteriorated 😞. It’s just not the same anymore, and it’s disappointing to see the quality drop. Hope they bring back the original flavors they were known for.

That said, this place still shines for its ambience ✨, and for newcomers, it might still feel impressive and worth the visit. But for me, my interest in visiting Lotus Cafe is slowly fading away 😕. I guess it’s a matter of having it too many times.

Still, for the overall experience, I’d rate it 4 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐.

A Vibrant Spot with a Kick: Blabber Juhu

​If you’re looking for a spot in Juhu that nails the "Instagrammable" aesthetic without sacrificing the quality of the meal, Blabber All Day is definitely worth a visit. Here is a breakdown of the experience:

​The Ambience
​The decor is easily the highlight. It’s elegant, whimsical, and filled with soft pastel hues and floral accents. Whether you’re looking for a brunch spot with friends or a cozy corner for a date, the atmosphere feels upscale yet welcoming. It’s one of those rare places where the lighting actually does you favors!

​The Food & Drink
​The menu is diverse, offering a great mix of global cuisines. The presentation is top-tier—everything from the cocktails to the dim sum arrives looking like a work of art.

​A Note on the Palate
​The food is undeniably high-quality, though it’s worth noting that the kitchen leans toward a bolder, spicier flavor profile.

​The Pro: The spices are fresh and aromatic, giving the dishes a real "zing" that stands out.
​The Caution: If you have a lower spice tolerance, you might find some dishes a bit intense.

​Tip: Don't hesitate to ask the servers to dial back the heat when you order; they are quite accommodating! Pairing your meal with one of their signature mocktails or shakes also helps balance out the fire.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Blabber All Day recently and had a great experience overall! One of the major plus points is their valet parking facility, which makes things so much easier in a busy area like this.

We had a reservation via Zomato, and thankfully we did—because the place was fully packed! Booking in advance really helped us avoid the wait.

Once seated, the service was very attentive. A modern touch I appreciated was that there’s no physical menu—each table has a QR code you can scan to order directly, including for cocktails, appetizers, and mains. Another thoughtful feature is the “ring for service” button on each table, which alerts the staff directly instead of having to call them over repeatedly—very convenient!

The ambience is chic and aesthetic, with dim lighting and a peaceful vibe, perfect for a relaxed evening.

Here’s what we ordered:
•	Cheesy Stuffed Mushrooms – Juicy with mild, flavorful stuffing. A good start.
•	Crackling Rolls (Sushi) – Absolutely mind-blowing! So good that we reordered.
•	Edamame Truffle Dim Sum – Wasn’t a fan of this one. It looked good but lacked the punch.
•	Berry Smoke Cocktail – Great presentation and a refreshing mix of berries and herbs.
•	Spaghetti Aglio Olio with Pepperoni – Taste was decent, but it was on the drier side.

The staff was friendly and efficient, making the entire experience smooth and enjoyable. I’d definitely recommend this place for a date night, an evening out with friends, family get-togethers, or even colleague dinners.

Tip: Make a reservation in advance to avoid waiting, and if you’re booking via Zomato, you can also avail 20% off when you pay through the app.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Third Wave Café in Vile Parle just yesterday, and while there were a few highlights, the overall experience left room for improvement.

Parking:
One of the first challenges we faced was parking. There’s no dedicated parking for the café, and you’re left to hunt for a spot nearby. With MTP odd-even parking rules in place, it gets even trickier. Be cautious — incorrect parking here can lead to hefty fines from the Maharashtra Traffic Police.

Ambience & Crowd:
When we entered, the café wasn’t too crowded — just a couple of tables were occupied. So, we expected a smooth and quick service experience.

Service:
Unfortunately, the service was disappointing. Despite the café being nearly empty, we had to wait 20–25 minutes for our order. The staff seemed distracted and unresponsive — even when we tried to call them over, it felt like they were in their own world. This slow and inattentive service really took away from the overall experience, especially since we were quite hungry.

Food:
On the brighter side, the food was excellent. We ordered the Chicken Tikka Roll and Paneer Tikka Roll — both were served in good quantity and tasted delicious. The flavors were spot on, and the food was definitely the highlight of our visit.

Final Thoughts:
If you’re visiting for the food, you won’t be disappointed — it’s tasty and filling. But be prepared for slow service and no parking options. Hopefully, the management takes steps to improve the service quality, because the food truly deserves better support.

Pay and Park facility is available just besides the restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Happened to visit this place when the restaurant that we had a reservation couldn't give us a table. We really enjoyed our visit here. We had a veg club sandwich and a pink sauce pasta both well done. Service was moderately quick for food but faster for the desserts & coffee. We tried their donuts chocolate and lotus Biscoff variants which are both well made and served warm. Their cafe mocha however wasn't upto the mark. The coffee in itself seemed like a dark roast and there was nil chocolate flavour except for the topping of chocolate sauce in the cup. We would probably pass the coffee section next time. But their food and desserts are an absolute hit. The fries served alongside the sandwich were also fresh and seemed homemade and not frozen.
The ambience was good, lighting was bright and the seating was comfortable. There are ample tables available to choose from. Staff were warm, professional and welcoming. We had a fantastic experience at the outlet and are happy to have visited. Not sure if they have a valet for parking though.

featured_reviews.name: Sangram Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text: Food is delicious. Ambience is good. Service is very slow. And they are not Even though the place was not crowded. The kitchen staff seems to be understaffed. Wait staff werent bothered much. The barista boy was quick with our coffee order. The cut fruits ordered for our toddler, were not cleaned properly still had the remains of the sticker on it.

featured_reviews.name: Shweta
featured_reviews.review_text:
For a place that is known for cheesecake, I cannot understand why Poetry decided to fill its blueberry “cheesecake” with whipped cream. You know how to make cheesecakes (as evidenced by the apple crumble cheesecake we also ordered); so own it! Don’t stoop to the level of imitators who often pass off the blueberry “whipped cream cake” as an “authentic cheesecake” to the common Mumbaikar.

Next disappointment: the “mandarin” mojito which was actually a mosambi juice with no mandarin or mojito to be tasted.

Finally, a note to your chefs: from an avowed chili lover, more green chilies does not equal better taste, in fact it makes food inedible. Uncle Roger himself would be crying tears of fresh disappointment. We had to find and remove every green chili from the Asian rice bowl, and now we’re no longer sure what is a green chili, or a green onion, or a simple green bean. Don’t fall victim to this unfortunate restaurant trend. We believe in you!

Other than that, good flavours as always, great pesto chicken.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually don’t go out of my way to post negative reviews, but this experience left me quite disappointed. We had ordered tacos, and unfortunately, the shells were extremely undercooked so chewy that they wouldn’t even break despite trying hard to bite into them.

We politely informed the staff and even showed them the issue by breaking the tacos in front of them. However, instead of acknowledging our concern, we were told that “tacos are like this,” which honestly felt dismissive, as if we didn’t know what we were talking about. There was no attempt to understand our perspective. I even suggested that they try one themselves, and if they still felt it was fine, we wouldn’t pursue the complaint but that wasn’t considered.

Eventually, they offered a replacement, but by then the experience had already been affected, so we chose not to proceed. What added to the disappointment was that the uneaten tacos were left on our table and not cleared.

A bad dish can happen anywhere, but how it’s handled makes all the difference. Unfortunately, the lack of acknowledgment and response from the staff made the experience worse than it needed to be.

featured_reviews.review_text:
​Cohoma Coffee Company has carved out a sleek, modern niche in the Juhu coffee scene. It feels less like a standard cafe and more like a dedicated "experience center" for serious coffee enthusiasts. Here is a breakdown of what to expect:
The Vibe & Ambiance
The space is minimalist, bright, and impeccably clean. It leans into a contemporary aesthetic with industrial touches, making it an excellent spot for a focused work session or a quick, high-quality caffeine fix. While it may not have the "cozy armchair" feel of some neighborhood cafes, it makes up for it with a sophisticated, professional energy.
The Brews
Cohoma shines when it comes to the technical side of coffee. They offer a variety of brewing methods, including:
​Cold Brews: Smooth, low-acid, and consistently refreshing. Their flavored cold brews (like Vanilla or Roasted Hazelnut) are well-balanced without being cloyingly sweet.
​Pour-Overs: For those who appreciate the nuances of the bean, their pour-overs are clean and highlight the specific notes of their medium and dark roasts.
​Signature Lattes: They offer a great selection of plant-based milks, ensuring that their specialty lattes remain creamy and flavorful for those preferring dairy alternatives.
I had their Iced Hojicha Latte.. slightly bitter but a good alternative cold coffee! #Cohoma #Coffee #Company #Juhu

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Aegyo Cafe and honestly it’s one of the best places in Mumbai for Asian & Korean food 🇰🇷✨ The cafe has both indoor and outdoor seating, with a very comfortable and aesthetic vibe. What makes it even better is that it’s a 100% halal cafe with absolutely no alcohol and no pork, which is a big plus.
They’ve recently launched a new Stranger Things themed menu, and the concept is super fun and creative. We started with appetizers like Friends Don’t Lie Chicken – perfectly crispy and juicy – and the Crispy Roll, which was well-fried and full of flavour.
For mains, we tried the Vecna Burger (Veg) and it was surprisingly good, nicely loaded and very satisfying.
In beverages, the Lotus Biscoff Milk Boba was rich, creamy and perfect for Biscoff lovers, while the Raspberry Slurpee was refreshing and chilled.
The highlight for me was the Korean Chicken Bento Box – a complete Korean meal in one box with corn dog, chicken pieces, dip, chicken gravy, flat noodles and even a cake.
For dessert, we ended with Eggo, which had a waffle base topped with cream and strawberry – light, fresh and a perfect ending.
Overall, great food, unique theme and a must-visit cafe for Korean food lovers in Mumbai. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: sayama khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Aegyo Café, and it truly turned out to be one of the most charming and aesthetic cafés I’ve ever been to! The moment you step inside, the Korean-inspired ambiance instantly wins your heart — pastel décor, cozy corners, and such cheerful energy that lifts your mood right away. ✨

The staff was extremely polite and welcoming, and the service was smooth throughout our visit. Now coming to the best part — the food! Every dish we tried was beautifully plated, bursting with flavor, and carried its own unique twist.

We ordered the Chicken Yom Tom, Street Style Chicken Chilli, Chow Mein Bowl, and Pink Rice Bowl, along with Spring Rolls, a Belgian Chocolate Boba Shake, and a Strawberry Milkshake — and honestly, every single item was a hit! The Chicken Yom Tom had a comforting, mildly spicy taste that instantly stood out, while the Street Style Chicken Chilli was bold, tangy, and perfectly balanced. The bowls were hearty, wholesome, and packed with flavor — ideal for a fulfilling meal. 🍜

For desserts, we indulged in their Milk Cake, Assorted Mochi, and Churros, and it was the perfect sweet ending! The mochi was soft, chewy, and absolutely delightful — with just the right touch of sweetness. 🍡💖

Overall, everything about Aegyo Café felt so thoughtfully curated — from the presentation to the flavors, from the interiors to the service. It’s one of those cafés where you don’t just eat — you experience the vibe. Every corner is picture-perfect, every dish is delicious, and every moment feels joyful.

If you’re someone who loves exploring cute, aesthetic cafés with great food and good vibes, Aegyo Café deserves a top spot on your list! 🌸✨

featured_reviews.name: Mohak Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place recently and had a pleasant overall experience. The café has a very welcoming atmosphere with tasteful interiors and good music playing in the background, making it a comfortable spot to relax or catch up with friends.

I tried the Vietnamese cold coffee, which was decent but fairly average in terms of taste. The Korean cheese garlic bun, on the other hand, was excellent — soft, buttery, and nicely balanced with garlic and cheese flavors. Definitely the highlight of the order and something I would recommend trying.

I also ordered the mozzarella fries. While the texture was crispy and the portion was good, the seasoning felt a little mild and slightly low on salt. The dip served alongside didn’t complement the fries very well, which made the dish feel slightly underwhelming.

One thing that truly stood out was the service. The staff was courteous, attentive, and quick, which added a lot to the overall experience.

Overall, a nice café with a great vibe and good hospitality. With a few small improvements in seasoning and dip pairings, the food could easily match the quality of the ambience.

⭐ Rating suggestion: 3.8–4.0/5 (honest but fair)

We tried at delicious food like 🍓Strawberry Matcha Cloud- which is refreshing, creamy, and perfectly balanced. 🧋French Vanilla Frappe-smooth and rich, 🍜 Spicy Chicken Ramen Bowl – a comforting bowl of warmth, best 🍱 Korean Bento Box -a complete meal and my favorite! It came with flat noodles, crispy chicken, flavorful chicken katsu gravy, corn dog, tasty dip, and the best milk cake dessert i ever had. Everything was beautifully served and full of flavor. 🧆KKANPUNGI- totally love it 🍤Shrimp Tempura Roll (Sushi)-crispy, light, and just melt-in-the-mouth. 🥟Mandu- juicy dumplings pack with flavour, Jiggly Cat Jelly-the cutest and must try dessert!
The service was quick, the staff super friendly, and the vibe totally aesthetic. Every corner of the café is picture-perfect, ideal for a cozy date or a cute hangout! and for family time too✨

featured_reviews.name: Riya
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited Cafe Aegyo and the experience was amazing. We were so happy with the deliciousness of their food and amazing service. I tried few items from their new menu as well. For drinks we got Strawberry Matcha Cloud and Vanilla Cold Foam and both the drinks were perfectly balanced, sweet and amazing. For appetisers, we got Street Style Chicken Chilli which was so tender, spicy and yum. Also got Spicy honey chilli fries which I tried for the first time and it was tangy, sweet and spicy. For mains, I had to get their Korean Fried Chicken Burger and it was juicy, flavourful and so tender. My fav part was their Jiggly Cake Pudding which was soft and together with the popping boba was an excellent combination. Also took a takeaway of their Gimbap, which was so delicious. The cafe has lots of other amazing items and the interiors have a korean touch. Definitely would recommend to visit this place.

featured_reviews.name: Anusha Suvarna
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aegyo cafe was the perfect dine in spot for my Sunday dinner. Cozy vibes, perfect playlist and music loud enough to be enjoyed without having to scream across the table to have a conversation.

The food and service were bang on! We ordered the katsu chicken sando (YUM!), katsu curry (best I’ve had since my trip to Japan), miso ramen and long fries. The flavours were perfect and kept me going back for more. We paired this meal with their iced frappe and we couldn’t stop at 1. So good!

For dessert, do try the mochi ice cream.

Overall, the staff is really warm and the vibe of the place is perfect for a date night. The cherry blossom decor looks great for a photo op. Will definitely keep going back for more meals here!

featured_reviews.name: Veeni Saumil Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a cozy, feel-good cafe in Bandra–Khar, Cafe Aegyo is such a happy little spot. The decor is super quirky, pastel and aesthetic, cute corners and a very comforting vibe. It instantly feels like a warm hug kind of place… perfect for catching up with friends, cute dates, or even a peaceful solo coffee + work day.

They’ve introduced a new Pan-Asian menu and I loved how comforting and flavourful everything tasted.

We tried
• Veg Shanghai – paneer lovers, this one’s for you! Tangy, saucy and super flavourful.

• Veg Gyoza – soft, nicely filled dumplings with a lovely dipping sauce. Simple yet so satisfying.

• Pad Thai Noodles – that sweet-tangy Thai flavour, nicely balanced with peanuts and veggies. Comfort in a bowl

• Chilli Garlic Fried Rice with Gravy – this was total comfort food! Spicy, garlicky and so wholesome when mixed with the gravy.

And of course… Boba time
• Lotus Biscoff Milky Brew is like dessert in a cup, rich, creamy and indulgent.

• Passion Fruit Boba is fresh, fruity and perfect if you prefer something lighter.

For dessert, we ended with their Strawberry Milk Cake and it was such a pretty and delicious end .. soft, moist and really fresh.

Overall, it’s a cute aesthetic cafe with good comforting food, great vibes and friendly energy. Definitely one of those places you’d want to come back to when you want something cozy and happy.

We ordered a cold coffee, piña colada, sunrise mocktail, and a plate of pita bread with hummus. Everything tasted fresh and was genuinely refreshing. The ambiance and setting added a lot to the experience, especially with the sun going down in the background.

That said, while the overall experience was enjoyable, the pricing felt a bit steep—₹250 for a tea or ₹100 for plain toasted bread, for example. Our total bill came to around ₹2,000, which didn’t quite match up to what we ordered. So, while it’s definitely worth trying once for the view and vibe, a little more balance in the pricing would make it even better.

featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text: The Conservatory stands out for its ambience and experience and It is one of Juhu's most aesthetically designed restaurants, featuring a glasshouse-style structure filled with greenery, natural light, a calm atmosphere, relaxed music levels and comfortable seating perfect for Casual brunches, Date nights, Long catch-ups with friends, Solo coffee sessions and work meetings during quieter hours. The menu is eclectic, covering Continental, Asian-inspired dishes, pizzas, salads, and café-style comfort food. Top dishes include Pesto Burrata Pizza, Avocado Smash Toast, Pita & Black bean hummus, Watermelon feta salad, Chocolate Gateaux in dessert. The food is fresh, tasty and plated well. Cocktails are often highlighted as a strong point. Loved its Berry wishper and Liit. The drinks are well-balanced and visually appealing. The service is  friendly and attentive. The Conservatory is one of Juhu's strongest choices when you value ambience, greenery, cocktails, and a leisurely dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Divya Dangwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Conservatory in Juhu recently, and the experience was absolutely lovely. Known for its contemporary Italian and North Indian menu, the place perfectly blends great food with a stunning ambience.

We started with the Phuket salad and kimchi broccoli — both were incredibly delicious and full of unique flavours. The appetisers were definitely a standout.

For mains, we tried the spaghetti in arrabbiata sauce, which was rich, creamy, and perfectly done, along with the pesto burrata pizza that was equally impressive. The portion sizes were quite generous and easily sufficient for two people.

Their house special cocktails are a must-try, especially the “Berry Nice To Meet You,” which was refreshing and beautifully crafted.

What truly elevates the experience is the ambience — super chic, classy, and elegant with a rustic touch. The beautiful glass roof setup adds a very aesthetic and sophisticated charm to the place.

Overall, Conservatory is a perfect spot for good food, cocktails, and a beautifully curated dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:

We started with their cocktails Lucent Ruby and Berry Nice to Meet You and both were super refreshing with well-balanced flavours.

For food, the roasted chicken salad was fresh and wholesome, while the black hummus pita was creamy, rich, and paired perfectly together. The char grilled prawns were flavourful and cooked really well, and the chicken pepperoni pizza was cheesy, comforting, and easily one of our favourites from the table.

Overall, the place nails the combination of good food, great cocktails, and a relaxing atmosphere. Definitely a spot worth visiting when you’re in the mood for a chill outing with friends or family.

featured_reviews.name: Arjika S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited The Conservatory in Juhu recently, and it turned out to be a really pleasant experience overall.

The ambience is one of the biggest highlights of this place. It’s calm, green, and thoughtfully designed — a refreshing break from the usual crowded and noisy café scenes in Mumbai. The seating is comfortable, the vibe is peaceful, and it’s perfect for slow meals, long conversations, or even solo visits if you just want to unwind.

We started with drinks, and both were quite refreshing. The Blushing Garden was light and well-balanced, while the Honey Wood Fyzz had a subtle sweetness that made it easy to sip and enjoy without feeling overpowering.

For starters, we tried the Whole Boneless Chicken Wing, Smoked Charcoal Chicken, and the Cream Cheese Bun. The chicken dishes were juicy, flavourful, and cooked well, especially the smoked preparation which had a nice depth of flavour. The Cream Cheese Bun was soft, comforting, and a good addition if you like mild, creamy flavours.

Moving on to the mains, the Zataar Chicken Pizza stood out. It was herby, satisfying, and filling without being too heavy — ideal to share.

We ended the meal with dessert, opting for the Chocolate Gateaux. Rich, indulgent, and not overly sweet, it was a great way to finish the meal.

The pricing is slightly on the premium side, but the quality of food, presentation, and especially the ambience justify it. Service was polite and attentive without being intrusive.

Overall, The Conservatory is a great choice if you’re looking for a peaceful café in Juhu with good food and a relaxed atmosphere. Definitely worth visiting if you enjoy calm spaces and thoughtfully prepared dishes.
